narrative.headline: High Tight Flag (Powerplay) - 107.2% pole in 40 bars + 6-bar flag retracing 19.6%. Pivot $20.05, target $30.47, R:R 4.5.
narrative.what_it_is: The High Tight Flag, originally identified by William O'Neil and popularized by Pradeep Bonde of Stockbee, is the rarest and most explosive continuation pattern in technical analysis. It requires a near-vertical advance of at least 90% in 8 weeks or less - a move so violent it can only come from a sudden change in fundamentals (FDA approval, earnings surprise, acquisition speculation, regulatory breakthrough) combined with restricted supply. The 'flag' that follows is not a normal pullback - it's a tight, orderly consolidation where buyers refuse to sell at lower prices and supply is exhausted. The 107.2% pole here over 40 bars represents extraordinary institutional accumulation, and the 6-bar flag at 19.6% retrace with volume contracted to 38% of pole average shows the consolidation is shallow and orderly - exactly the signature O'Neil and Bonde teach. Historically, when HTF triggers cleanly on a volume surge, the next 8-12 weeks frequently produce 100%+ extensions, making this the highest reward-to-risk continuation setup that exists on the chart. This matches the momentum-breakout structure Kristjan Kullamägi describes on his own site: a leader up 30-100%+ in the prior 1-3 months, consolidating 2 weeks to 2 months while riding a rising 10- and 20-day average, that then expands out of the range on volume. He sizes setups like this 5-25% of account (most around 10-15%), scaled by the stock's liquidity and his conviction, with risk capped near 0.25-1% of account and a stop no wider than the stock's own ADR.
narrative.why_it_matters: This HTF is forming in a confirmed Stage 2 uptrend with fully stacked-bullish moving-average alignment and improving relative strength versus the broader market. The 107.2% pole over 40 bars - exceptional even by HTF standards - implies a fundamental catalyst of significant magnitude that the market is still pricing in, because moves this violent only come from genuine paradigm shifts in earnings power or supply/demand. Volume contraction in the flag to 38% of pole average is the key tell: supply is being absorbed by patient institutional buyers, not distributed by trapped longs. The 19.6% retrace is shallow enough that profit-takers haven't broken the institutional pattern, yet (where applicable) deep enough to shake out late-momentum chasers who bought near the pole top. Within the bullish regime, HTFs are particularly potent - they signal the names that institutional desks are aggressively building positions in regardless of broader tape, and these are the setups that historically dominate Investor's Business Daily leaderboards. Higher low confirmed — pullback low ($18.04) is 86.2% above the prior swing low ($9.69). Strong uptrend structure. Pullback low sits 0.68% above rising 21-EMA (Minervini's primary support) ($17.92). Strong MA-pullback alignment.
narrative.what_to_watch_for: The trigger is a daily close above $20.07 (flag high $20.05 plus a small confirmation buffer) on volume of 2x or more the 20-bar average - HTF requires EXPLOSIVE volume confirmation, not the 1.5x threshold that suits standard patterns, because the entire setup is built on institutional urgency. The ideal trigger bar closes in the upper third of its range with a wide bar (high - low > 1.5x ATR) and prints a gap or near-gap open. Measured target is $30.47 (pole height of $10.39 projected from flag high), but the most aggressive HTF practitioners (Bonde) teach a 2x pole projection at $40.86 for the strongest cases - both targets often hit within 6-10 weeks when the breakout works. Trail stops below each new swing low as the stock advances; HTFs frequently retest the flag region once before extending, so the first stop should be wide enough to survive that retest, and add-on entries should be reserved for clean continuation rather than chase trades into extended bars.
narrative.failure_signal: The HTF is invalidated if price closes below the flag low at $18.04 (stop set at $17.77, ~1.5% below the structural low to give room for the standard flush). Critically, a fade off the entry on weak volume or a failed first 1-2 days IS the failure mode - HTFs that don't gap or close strongly into the breakout usually do not work, because the entire setup is predicated on institutional buying being unmistakably aggressive on the trigger. The penalty for being wrong on an HTF is severe because position sizes are typically larger relative to standard patterns (the 90%+ pole has stretched volatility and operators are tempted to size up for the asymmetric reward), so disciplined stops are non-negotiable. A failed HTF often retests a much deeper support level (50-bar low or back to the pre-pole base near $9.69), so honor the 11.5% stop and do NOT widen it on the way down - sizing for a 1% account risk implies roughly 9% of equity per trade, which is already aggressive given the volatility profile.
